classification.difficultyReason: Apply Pythagoras to two given perpendicular sides and round the hypotenuse to two decimal places.

content.prompt: Find the length of the hypotenuse, correct to 2 decimal places, in the triangle below.

spec.description: Right triangle with equal vertical and horizontal legs, matching single ticks, a bottom-left right-angle mark and descending hypotenuse. Decorative source blue is replaced with house black.
spec.mathematics: Both perpendicular legs measure 3 m; the hypotenuse is labelled x m.
spec.answerVisibility: Only supplied measurements and the unknown label are visible.

answer.worked:
By Pythagoras’ theorem:
$$\begin{align*}x^2&=3^2+3^2\\x^2&=9+9\\x^2&=18\\x&=\sqrt{18}\\x&\approx4.24\text{ m}\quad\text{(2 decimal places).}\end{align*}$$
